source_findings.finding: Codex work spans app, CLI, IDE, and cloud surfaces, so multi-surface status continuity needs shared receipts.
source_findings.application: Keep app and CLI lanes normalized through one five-lane board before phase advancement.

source_findings.finding: Codex surfaces change quickly enough that helper behavior should be receipt-driven and modular.
source_findings.application: Prefer small watcher, classifier, normalizer, and dashboard receipts over broad runtime rewrites.

source_findings.finding: Safe agent operation benefits from layered controls, constrained tool use, and clear review boundaries.
source_findings.application: Use exact gates, redaction, exposure checks, and status-only publication for sibling outputs.

source_findings.finding: Least authority and confused-deputy avoidance are central for connector and tool orchestration.
source_findings.application: Keep external and connector surfaces read-scoped unless an exact live mutation packet exists.

source_findings.source: OWASP Logging and Secrets Management cheat sheets
source_findings.finding: Diagnostics can leak secrets or private context if raw material is published.
source_findings.application: Publish hashes, counts, pass/fail states, and sanitized summaries instead of raw lane text or logs.

x2_build_implications: Make watcher trust explicit: do not check sibling status before configured x1 and x2 marks.
Carry app redaction before app gate as a serial safety invariant.
Use quality gates to distinguish real CLI blockers from false-positive generic marker warnings.
Turn Arby and Aster Vale long-form outputs into x2 build queue items without publishing raw text.
Keep GMUT, canon, consciousness, and final-physics gates open unless exact closure artifacts exist.
